steps.label: det(A) = ad - bc for A = [[a,b],[c,d]]
steps.sub: A has an inverse if and only if det(A) != 0

steps.label: Inverse formula: swap a & d, negate b & c, divide by det

caption: Determinant nonzero, so the inverse exists — confirmed by actually multiplying A by its inverse to recover the identity.

eyebrow: Why Every Gate Must Be Invertible

steps.label: det = 0 would mean dividing by zero
steps.sub: The inverse formula breaks down — no inverse exists

steps.label: Geometrically, det 0 squashes the plane onto a line
steps.sub: Different inputs can land on the same output — information is gone

steps.label: Quantum computation never destroys information
steps.sub: Every valid gate matrix must have determinant nonzero

subtitle: Shapes that are easy to compute with and map onto real physical structure.
